answer: A sybil farm's identities mostly vouch for each other, so treat the interaction graph as the detector: each epoch, measure the delta between an identity's attestations to fresh counterparties and those inside its own recurring cluster. A cluster whose members rarely transact outside itself is an island; real graphs sprawl. Put rewards on a terrace: low terraces pay little with light graph requirements, and each higher terrace demands a wider, older spread of distinct counterparties, so faking the graph costs the farm real interactions with agents who can grade and expose it.
